html:
Messene was founded in 369 BCE on the slopes of Mount Ithome in the southwest Peloponnese, as the new capital of the Messenians, just freed from centuries of Spartan rule.

Sparta had conquered Messenia in the 8th and 7th centuries BCE, in wars such as the Second Messenian War, and turned its people into helots, serfs who farmed the land for Spartan masters. Helot labour was what let Spartan men train full time for war. After his victory at the Battle of Leuctra, Epaminondas of Thebes invaded, freed the helots of Messenia and called home Messenians whose families had lived in exile for generations.

He built them a city with huge stone walls, about 9 km around, which are among the best preserved Greek fortifications today. Messene was meant to keep Sparta in check, together with the new Arcadian city of Megalopolis. It worked: without Messenia's land and labour, Sparta never again was a great power. The ruins of the city, with its theatre, stadium and gates, have been excavated since the 1980s.
sum: Messene was founded in 369 BCE on the slopes of Mount Ithome in the southwest Peloponnese, as the new capital of the Messenians, just freed from centuries of Spartan rule.
